title: Environmental Specialist III
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Environmental Specialist III is an advanced individual contributor responsible for independently leading complex environmental compliance work across assigned company facilities and business areas. This role develops, maintains, evaluates, and improves environmental programs, plans, permits, records, training, reports, and regulatory submissions. The position serves as a practical compliance resource for operations, Environmental Quality (EQ) team members, regulators, consultants, vendors, and internal stakeholders. The Environmental Specialist III is expected to manage higher-risk or more complex compliance matters with minimal direction, provide guidance to Environmental Specialist I and II team members, and help standardize workflows, tools, and records so compliance work is accurate, timely, and defensible.

This position is based on-site in Appleton, WI with a hybrid work schedule (Monday - Thursday on-site). Minimal travel and after hours / on call support is also required.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Environmental Program Leadership and Facility Support

  • Develop, evaluate, and improve environmental compliance programs, including Environmental Management System (EMS) and Environmental Information Management System (EIMS) tools.
  • Serve as the environmental lead or advanced support resource for assigned facilities, business units, or programs.
  • Identify compliance gaps, evaluate risks, and recommend practical corrective actions.
  • Track inspections, compliance tasks, deadlines, open items, and required documentation.
  • Support operating divisions and align local practices with company expectations.

Regulatory Reporting, Permitting, and Agency Support

  • Prepare, review, and submit required environmental reports, including air, water, waste, Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (EPCRA), Toxic Release Inventory (TRI), and other regulatory submissions.
  • Prepare, coordinate, and maintain permits, licenses, registrations, approvals, exemptions, renewals, and notifications.
  • Lead or support agency communications, responses, follow-up, and correspondence tracking.
  • Coordinate submission logistics, signatures, certifications, portal uploads, mailing, and tracking.
  • Maintain regulator-ready files, calculations, assumptions, and supporting records.

Plans, Preparedness, and Spill Response

  • Write, update, and maintain environmental plans, including Facility Response Plans (FRPs), Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure (SPCC) Plans, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs), waste plans, contingency plans, and related emergency response documents.
  • Support Oil Pollution Act of 1990 (OPA-90) planning, Qualified Individual updates, drills, certifications, and plan submissions.
  • Support spill response, incident documentation, corrective actions, lessons learned, and internal communication.
  • Update plans after personnel, equipment, process, facility, product, regulatory, or operational changes.
  • Keep emergency planning documents current, complete, accessible, and response-ready.

Air, Water, Waste, Tank, and Vapor Control Compliance

  • Lead or support air permitting, emissions calculations, reporting, stack testing, vapor control compliance, agency notifications, and test report review.
  • Support emissions monitoring requirements, including Continuous Emissions Monitoring System (CEMS), Relative Accuracy Test Audit (RATA), and Cylinder Gas Audit (CGA) obligations.
  • Lead or support water compliance, including National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES), stormwater, sampling, corrective actions, and Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) reporting.
  • Manage hazardous waste, universal waste, and recycling compliance, including profiles, manifests, vendors, and disposal records.
  • Maintain tank compliance records, including inspections, service status, vapor tightness, test records, and supporting permit or SPCC documentation.

Audits, Inspections, Corrective Actions, and Risk Management

  • Arrange, conduct, or support environmental audits of company facilities, contractors, and waste handlers.
  • Prepare for regulatory inspections, coordinate responses, and track follow-up actions to completion.
  • Communicate deficiencies and corrective actions clearly to reduce risk and improve compliance.
  • Support environmental risk reviews for business continuity, insurance, sustainability, and enterprise risk needs.
  • Develop tools, templates, and checklists for audits, inspections, corrective actions, and recurring compliance tasks.
  • Support DOT hazardous materials compliance, Process Safety Management (PSM), Risk Management Plan (RMP), and United States Coast Guard (USCG) compliance including cyber security, by managing records, plans, inspections, audits, corrective actions, and regulatory coordination.

Data, Digital Tools, Records, and Process Improvement

  • Maintain environmental records according to retention and document management requirements.
  • Maintain and improve SharePoint sites, trackers, Microsoft Lists, dashboards, spreadsheets, databases, and related compliance tools.
  • Improve workflows, data quality, visibility, and follow-up for environmental compliance work.
  • Coordinate environmental data requests for internal stakeholders.
  • Standardize work, improve quality control, and prevent missed deadlines or inconsistent records.

Training, Mentoring, and Subject Matter Support

  • Create, conduct, or coordinate environmental training for associates, contractors, and facility personnel.
  • Verify training completion and follow up on overdue or incomplete assignments.
  • Mentor Environmental Specialist I and II team members and develop practical guidance, templates, and checklists.
  • Support the Subject Matter Expert (SME) structure by researching requirements, providing input, and engaging SMEs when needed.
  • Communicate technical requirements in clear, practical language for operations and other stakeholders.

Projects, Vendors, Remediation, and Due Diligence

  • Arrange and oversee environmental vendors, consultants, inspections, testing, emergency response, software, and remediation services.
  • Coordinate remediation, investigations, corrective actions, cleanup projects, and liability tracking.
  • Support acquisition and divestiture environmental reviews, including Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments and due diligence.
  • Review consultant and vendor deliverables for completeness, quality, and submission readiness.
  • Support environmental review of facility, construction, tank, vapor control, product, equipment, and operational changes.

Values, Continuous Improvement, and Other Duties

  • Demonstrate U.S. Venture values in daily work and decision-making.
  • Identify ways to improve efficiency, accuracy, consistency, standardization, and quality control.
  • Maintain current knowledge of environmental regulations, permits, operations, and compliance technology.
  • Support safety, government compliance, and company policies and procedures.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned. These responsibilities are representative and are not intended to be all-encompassing.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Biology, Geology/Earth Science, Safety, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered where appropriate.
  • 4 to 7 years or more of environmental compliance, regulatory agency, environmental specialist, or equivalent experience; or 5 or more years of relevant experience with a credential such as Engineer in Training (EIT), Professional Engineer (PE), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), Registered Environmental Manager (REM), or a related certification.
  • Ability to independently complete environmental reports, permits, plans, inspections, records, corrective action follow-up, and agency responses with minimal assistance.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret and apply environmental regulations, permits, plans, reports, technical guidance, and internal procedures.
  • Experience communicating environmental requirements to operations, management, contractors, regulators, consultants, and other stakeholders.
  • Strong written communication skills, with the ability to prepare regulator-ready correspondence, summaries, procedures, and compliance documentation.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to review work for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and defensibility before internal or external submission.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, especially Word, Excel, Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, and electronic document management or tracking tools.
  • Ability to travel to facilities, support inspections or audits, work with operations, and manage multiple deadlines across assigned sites or programs.
  • Successfully pass a pre-employment drug test, per company practice.

Corporate

title: Senior Specialist, Clinical Supplies Quality
description:
Job Description

This position reports to the Associate Director/Director, Global Clinical Supplies Quality and is critical to maintaining the global clinical supply chain via disposition activities for clinical finished goods provided by our Company for worldwide clinical trials.Specifically, this includes batch documentation review ensuring our clinical supplies are in compliance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMPs) regulations and relevant regulatory filing submissions.


Areas of focus of this position revolve around the detailed workings of clinical packaging, labeling and distribution activities and associated regulatory submissions for Investigational New Drug applications and Clinical Trial Applications in relation to complex/niche supply chains and supply types for clinical protocols as well as Managed Access Programs, Joint Ventures/Collaborations, Independent Investigator-Initiated Studies, etc.

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

  • Evaluation and disposition of clinical supply materials with the assurance that the materials were produced in conformance to all applicable policies/procedures of our Company and compliance with all governing regulations.
  • Coordinate and/or support the preparation of procedures, processes and quality improvements.
  • Assists in the coordination of significant quality events including fact finding, investigation, coordination of clinical quarantine and recovery actions.
  • Collaboration across cross-functional and business areas to ensure robust processing, continuous improvement and cross-functional team building.
  • Providing on-the-floor coaching/guidance of operational and technical issues; providing immediate resolution on the shop floor to deviations and potential deviations.
  • Completing projects to improve the performance of our processes, including continuous process improvements, investigation Corrective/Preventative Actions (CAPAs), and value capture projects that seek to improve outcomes, reduce cost, or lower our processing cycle times.
  • Managing investigation, change request and project timelines to ensure key compliance and customer due dates are met; escalating any potential misses and develop remediation plans when possible.

Education:

  • Minimum of a Bachelor's degree with a technical emphasis in an appropriate scientific or engineering field.

Required Experience and Skills:

  • Minimum of 5 years experience in the pharmaceutical or equivalent industry Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) related field including Technical, Regulatory, Quality or Operations.
  • Familiarity with batch disposition (release) activities, operations, or regulatory filing activities.
  • Prior experience authoring, reviewing or approving investigations, deviation management support, and Corrective/Preventative Actions (CAPAs).
  • Background in quality control, quality assurance, auditing or regulatory affairs.
  • Attention to detail, flexibility and an awareness of production and quality control problems.
  • Effectiveness and creativity in approaching and solving quality and technical challenges.
  • In-depth working knowledge of cGMPs and of regulatory requirements as they apply to the pharmaceutical field or a related area.
  • Evidence of leadership skills coupled with highly developed oral and written communication skills, i.e., effective presentation of concepts and ideas, as well as interpersonal and conflict resolution skills.
  • Demonstrated teamwork skills including ownership and accountability.

Preferred Skills:

  • Ability to independently manage multiple priorities and projects.
  • Ability to lead and support teams of a cross-functional and multi-level nature, including senior management representatives.
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Knowledge of Lean Six Sigma and Project Management.
  • Knowledge and competency in ERP/MES, Document Management Systems, SAP, PowerPoint, Excel and Word.

title: Senior Solution Consultant
description:
About the Role

Do you love turning a prospect’s goals into a demo they can see themselves in? Envisio is looking for a Senior Solution Consultant to be the product and value expert on our sales team, partnering with Senior Account Executives to meet with prospects across the public sector, primarily in local government and higher education.

Envisio is one of Western Canada's fastest-growing software companies, named one of 2026's Top 100 GovTech companies. We partner with organizations across the public sector, including local governments, higher education institutions, K-12, healthcare, and nonprofits, to help them plan, execute, and deliver on their most important priorities.

You'll lead discovery-informed demonstrations, proof of concepts, and technical responses that show senior leaders how Envisio connects strategy, integrated planning, and performance management. This is a fantastic opportunity to strengthen democracy by helping public sector organizations build trust with their elected officials, boards, and communities.


The Role

  • Partner with Senior Account Executives as the product and value champion with prospects across the public sector, primarily local government and higher education, as well as K-12, healthcare, and nonprofits, articulating Envisio's value proposition
  • Join discovery sessions, team presentations, and requirement scoping sessions, and help navigate complex, multi-stakeholder buying processes and sales cycles
  • Research each prospect's strategic portfolio of work, including plans, performance data, projects, priorities, and use cases, to shape a tailored solution story
  • Deliver tailored, value-oriented demonstrations that speak to each audience: workflows and ease of use for staff, visibility and control for managers, and the strategic story and credibility for executives, councils, and boards
  • Lead the technical and solution content for formal proposals, RFPs/RFQs, security questionnaires, and technical responses
  • Build and present proof of concepts, preparing and loading prospects' plans and datasets with accuracy and database stability
  • Maintain current demo environments for each market vertical (local government, higher education, K-12, healthcare, and nonprofits)
  • Use Envisio's AI-assisted sales enablement workflows to prepare faster and keep quality high
  • Prepare for and lead product-related webinars and solution walkthroughs at online and in-person customer summits, conferences, and events
  • Acquire deep knowledge of Envisio products and services, with the ability to navigate every functional area of the platform
  • Stay highly competent in Envisio's product roadmap and implementation approach, and liaise with Product and Customer Success so what is promised matches what is delivered
  • Bring the Voice of Sales to Product by logging and prioritizing customer feedback to inform enhancements and the roadmap
  • Light travel required


Your Skills and Experience


  • 3–5+ years of experience as a solution consultant, sales engineer, pre-sales consultant, or similar role
  • Strong knowledge of the public sector, strategy, and performance management, gained through experience in public sector innovation, strategic planning, or performance management roles, with an understanding of local government and/or higher education
  • Familiarity with strategic planning cycles, integrated planning, performance management, and data analytics
  • Strong presentation skills and comfort presenting to senior leaders and large audiences, including elected officials, boards, and executive teams
  • Able to design and present technical concepts and specific solutions clearly to audiences of varying technical capabilities
  • Experience supporting proposals, RFPs, and proof of concepts
  • Able to support multiple Senior Account Executives and multiple opportunities with varying requirements at the same time
  • Experience or level of familiarity with data analytics, business intelligence (BI), and project management tools
  • Hands-on experience with AI tools such as Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI (ChatGPT), including using them to research, build demos and prototypes, and speed up proposal and RFP work, plus the ability to speak credibly with public sector leaders about responsible AI use
  • Excellent analytical, written, verbal communication, and documentation skills
  • Bachelor's degree required

Key Attributes

  • Solution-oriented, self-motivated, creative, and detail-oriented
  • Direct and convincing when it's right for the customer, and credible and consultative with senior stakeholders
  • A natural storyteller who makes complex ideas visual and easy to understand
  • Genuine curiosity about client challenges and how we can help
  • Comfortable working independently and collaboratively, and able to stay focused and flexible during rapid change
  • High integrity and accountability
  • A passion for the public sector, higher education, and strengthening democracy


Why This Role?

You'll be the person who helps senior public sector leaders see what better planning, execution, and performance management looks like for their organization. You'll work closely with Account Executives in local government and higher education, and with Product and Customer Success, to make sure every promise we make is one we can deliver.

You'll be supported by a close-knit, highly collaborative sales and marketing team that wants you to succeed. We're looking for a self-starter, but you won't be doing it alone.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Extended health, dental and vision care
  • Vacation & paid time off


Why Envisio?

We're passionate about building deep, personalized relationships with our customers to help them become champions in strategic planning and execution. We are a true partner and trusted advisor, with a deep understanding of the public sector and a genuine interest in seeing every customer succeed. This is a remote role, with an office in downtown Vancouver, British Columbia, if you prefer to work in person. If you're looking for a fulfilling environment to grow professionally and personally, we think you'll like it here.

We'd love for you to join us!

title: Onboarding Experience Manager
description:
Onboarding Manager

As an Onboarding Experience Manager at Intiveo, you’ll be the first impression and trusted guide for our new clients. You are the first trusted partner clients work with after signing, guiding them from the initial kickoff through full adoption of our Patient Engagement platform.

You’ll translate big goals into actionable steps, build strong relationships, and show clients how Intiveo can elevate their workflow, efficiency, and overall patient journey. Your focus is to reduce “time to value,” ensure a seamless transition into the platform, and equip clients with the workflows, knowledge, and confidence they need to achieve their business goals. Success in this role means delivering best-in-class onboarding, driving early product adoption, and building strong client advocacy from day one.

Who Are We
Intiveo is a leading cloud-based patient engagement platform used by 15,000 practitioners to communicate with over 18 million patients. Our goal is to continuously improve patient care by understanding communication needs, behaviors, and preferences – resulting in successful treatment outcomes.

✨What You'll Do

  • Own & Lead the Onboarding Journey
    • Manage a portfolio of new client onboardings, delivering a structured, predictable, and delightful onboarding experience.
    • Create customized onboarding plans based on the client’s goals, practice workflows, and operational requirements.
    • Conduct meetings, establish clear expectations, define success metrics, and guide clients through each onboarding milestone.

  • Train & Empower Clients
    • Provide best practices that increase adoption and enable clinics to become self-sufficient power users.
    • Demonstrate how Intiveo enhances clinic efficiency, patient communication, and end-to-end experience.
    • Deliver high-impact product training tailored to each customer’s role, workflows, and business strategy.

  • Optimize Configuration & Platform Setup
    • Ensure accounts are configured for maximum efficiency, accuracy, and alignment with the patient journey.
    • Audit account setups for gaps, recommend enhancements, and implement improvements.

  • Drive Early Adoption & Time-to-Value
    • Use onboarding metrics, usage insights, and customer goals to accelerate adoption.
    • Identify potential risks early and proactively address barriers to ensure clients stay on track.
    • Conduct live customer satisfaction review meeting to present onboarding progress, gather feedback, and validate that clients are achieving their expected outcomes and ensure smooth transition to support.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
    • Collaborate with Sales to ensure alignment on client expectations, goals, and platform usage.
    • Partner with Tech Ops to manage escalations to resolve bugs or implementation issues.

  • Continuously Improve Onboarding Programs & Processes
    • Identify inefficiencies or gaps in the current onboarding workflow and recommend process improvements.

title: Assoc. Spclst, Quality Assurance
description:
Job Description

Role Summary:


Our Quality Assurance group ensures our products are manufactured, processed, tested, packaged, stored and distributed in alignment with our incredibly high standards of quality and meet all regulatory requirements. Partnering across our internal manufacturing facilities, external contract manufacturers and suppliers, we create an interdependent global manufacturing network committed to delivering a compliant, reliable supply to customers and patients on time, every time, across the globe.

The Quality Line Oversight Program at West Point is an entry level 2-year program with 8-month rotations focused on providing hands-on experience in pharmaceutical quality assurance supporting our Company’s largest and most complex vaccine manufacturing plant site. This entry level program provides individuals with a range of experiences across several core quality functions fostering a foundational introduction to the vaccine manufacturing business. This multi-faceted program supports opportunities to learn, upskill, and gain meaningful experience across different parts of vaccine manufacturing, facilitating future career development and job opportunities. The successful candidate will be part of the Quality Line Oversight Program as a Quality Associate Specialist located at the West Point, PA site. In addition to hands-on shopfloor experience, the employees will be provided with an exciting opportunity to participate in a quality rotational program. This program is designed such that employees will be assigned with appropriate mentors within various key areas of the Quality organization as part of the rotation. The employees will be provided training and shadowing opportunities and will gain exposure to tasks within key areas of quality, providing the employee with a broad view of the work at West Point At the completion of the QLO program including the rotations, successful individuals will be assigned to a Quality or Operations Specialist role to further develop the individual’s knowledge of the vaccine manufacturing business as well as help position them for future career growth.

The QLO Associate Specialist position is a direct manufacturing support role primarily on the shop floor within our Quality Line Oversight team. This team rotates through the vaccine filling and packaging departments at the West Point site providing quality and compliance oversight to our 24/7 manufacturing operations.


Primary Responsibilities:


  • Quality checks of finished product including visual inspection of vials, syringes and packages
  • Verification of appropriate line clearance between batches to prevent product mix-ups
  • GMP document / batch record review

Additional responsibilities:


  • Rotational support of Quality Assurance, Quality Operations, and Environmental Monitoring providing a foundational understanding of vaccine Quality oversight and production.
  • Continuous improvement projects by participating in problem solving and partnering with Operations, Technology, and/or other Quality groups in areas such as safety, quality, and efficiency

The shift structure for the position includes 12-hour day and night shifts which rotate approximately every 9 weeks. The position does require weekend coverage. Both the initial QLO assignment and future opportunities can include off-shift/off-schedule support within a vaccine manufacturing operations area.

This is an entry level position, and 0-2 years of experience in pharmaceutical industry through internships, co-operative education or other roles is preferred.


General Profile:


  • Contributes to the performance and results of a vaccine manufacturing department.
  • Provides regulatory, quality and compliance guidance.

Business Expertise:


  • Apply technical, collaboration and interpersonal skills to align activities with department objectives.

Functional Expertise:


  • Works as a team member on shop floor core tasks, quality systems activities and/or process improvement projects.
  • Has ability to examine an issue from perspectives (safety, compliance, automation, equipment, process, and people) in order to best understand and resolve the root cause.
  • Assures consistent application of standardized work, process tools, and procedures.
  • Assists with regulatory inspections in either documentation area, request management area or in the inspection room.
  • Provides quality guidance to technical and manufacturing documents necessary for investigations, process design/definition, engineering studies, process demonstrations, change control, and validation.
  • Effectively collaborates with peers on site and above site as required.

Education Minimum Requirement:


  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or sciences

Required Experience and Skills:


  • Willing to work alternate shifts and weekends.
  • Ability to focus on and obtain results
  • Good verbal and written communication skills
  • Ability to effectively collaborate within and across an integrated manufacturing team
  • Ability to enact conflict resolution
  • Ability to effectively respond to change
  • Excellent analytical and organizational skills
  • High personal integrity, credibility and energy
  • Flexibility to perform related tasks to support the business
  • Computer literacy in MS Office, Word, Outlook, Excel

Preferred Experience and Skills:


  • 0-2 years working experience in cGMP pharmaceutical environment
  • Experience using Lean/Six Sigma tools

Required Skills:

Analytical Problem Solving, Analytical Problem Solving, Aseptic Filling, Batch Record Review, cGMP Compliance, Complaint Management, Computer Literacy, Conflict Management, Continuous Improvement Techniques, Decision Making, Deviation Management, Engineering Document Management, Engineering Principle, Flexibility Training, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Microsoft Office, Pharmaceutical Industry, Quality Assurance (QA), Quality Auditing, Quality Management Standards, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Quality Standards, Quality Support, Regulatory Inspections, Regulatory Requirements {+ 10 more}

About the job:

We are seeking a highly skilled DevOps Specialist to architect, implement, and maintain end-to-end CI/CD pipelines using GitHub, with a strong focus on test-driven deployment, automated release management, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) practices.

The role also includes automating build, tagging, and publication processes across web, desktop, and mobile platforms to ensure consistent and traceable releases. Deep expertise in Linux system administration, networking, and IaC tools is essential to deliver

scalable, secure, and highly available deployments.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, architecture, and management of CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions (and similar tools), ensuring fast, reliable, and reproducible software delivery.
  • Implement and enforce test-driven deployment systems, integrating automated testing, validation, and monitoring to maintain code quality and accelerate feedback cycles.
  • Containerize applications and microservices with Docker, optimize image builds, and manage deployment pipelines for distributed environments.
  • Develop and maintain cross-platform build pipelines using CMake or equivalent tools, ensuring consistent compilation and release workflows across web, desktop, and mobile.
  • Automate end-to-end release processes, including tagging, building, signing, and distributing mobile, web, and desktop applications.
  • Define and manage Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to provision and maintain reliable, scalable, and secure infrastructure environments.
  • Collaborate closely with development, QA, and operations teams to troubleshoot deployment issues, optimize performance, and improve release reliability.
  • Continuously improve observability and feedback loops, leveraging monitoring and alerting systems to maintain operational excellence.

Mandatory:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience architecting and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions or equivalent tools at scale in a production environment.
  • Strong proficiency in test-driven deployment methodologies, including writing and maintaining automated test suites for integration and end-to-end validation.
  • Expertise in containerization technologies such as Docker, including image creation, registry management, and basic orchestration patterns.
  • In-depth knowledge of C++ build systems, specifically CMake, with proven experience optimizing native build and deployment pipelines.
  • Advanced Linux system administration and networking skills, including shell scripting, package management, performance troubleshooting, firewalls, and VPN configuration.
  • Excellent communication, problem-solving, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in globally distributed teams.
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Terraform, Ansible, AWS CDK or AWS CloudFormation.
  • Experience with mobile CI/CD automation, including build, tagging, and publication for iOS and Android applications
  • Advanced knowledge of release management practices, including automated versioning, signing, and artifact distribution.

title: Performance Engineer
description:
About the role

RNWBL is seeking a utility-scale Solar and BESS Performance Engineer to support the monitoring, analysis, and optimization of renewable energy assets across our solar and battery energy storage system (BESS) portfolio. The ideal candidate will have at least three years of relevant experience in renewable energy performance or a related field, a strong foundation in data analysis and scripting (Python or similar), and an interest in developing practical tools that improve performance engineering workflows.

The primary focus of this role will be utility-scale solar performance analysis, with opportunities to support wind projects as needs arise. Experience with BESS is a strong plus, particularly familiarity with battery system performance, availability, operating data, or related analytics. The Performance Engineer will work closely with Operations and Performance Engineering teams to deliver accurate, consistent, and actionable performance insights across the portfolio.

This role plays a critical part in automating analytics, developing and improving internal tools, maintaining data quality, and identifying operational issues that impact asset availability and energy production.

Key Responsibilities

· Analyze operational and performance data from utility-scale solar and BESS assets, with occasional support for wind projects

· Develop, execute, maintain, and improve Python-based scripts and other analytical tools used for performance monitoring, diagnostics, and reporting

· Support monthly and annual performance reporting, including data validation, KPI calculations, and investigation of data-quality issues

· Identify and quantify performance losses related to availability, curtailment, equipment outages, operating constraints, and environmental conditions

· Collaborate with Operations to investigate anomalies, support root-cause analysis, and translate findings into actionable recommendations

· Build and improve tools that automate repetitive reporting, data processing, and performance analysis tasks to improve efficiency and consistency

· Maintain clear documentation of code, scripts, analytical methodologies, data sources, and performance assumptions

· Contribute to the design and continuous improvement of internal performance engineering tools, dashboards, templates, and workflows

· Clearly communicate analytical findings, assumptions, and conclusions to customers through written reports and discussions

· Participate in team meetings and provide clear updates on assigned analyses, development work, and project tasks

Qualifications

· Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Data Science, Computer Science, Environmental Science, or a related technical field

· At least 3 years of experience in renewable energy, preferably in utility-scale solar performance, BESS, power systems, data analytics, or a related technical role

· Working proficiency in Python (required), with an interest in developing and maintaining code-based tools

· Familiarity with SQL, version control (Git), APIs, or cloud-based data environments preferred

· Experience working with time-series data, large datasets, and operational or SCADA data

· Familiarity with data visualization and dashboard tools (e.g., Power BI) is a plus

· Experience supporting or analyzing utility-scale BESS assets is a strong plus

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills

· Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams

Eligibility Requirements

· Must be authorized to work in the United States

· Ability to work in a hybrid environment in our Tempe location is a plus

· Willingness to occasionally support time-sensitive operational analyses

Physical Requirements

· Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer

· Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds occasionally

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid holidays and vacation time
  • Career Growth Opportunities within Wind, Solar, and BESS sectors
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Continuous Professional Development Support

title: Property Manager

The Property Manager is responsible for the overall performance of the community, including leasing success, resident satisfaction, financial performance, team leadership, property operations, and asset preservation.


The ideal candidate is an engaging leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, understands the importance of resident experience, and is committed to maintaining a community residents are proud to call home.

Property Operations

title: Senior Director of Philanthropy and Partnerships
description:
Are you committed to advancing economic equity and connecting underrepresented talent to career opportunities using mentorship and access to professional networks? Are you ready to drive growth and scale impact in service of a meaningful mission?

Organization Overview:

StreetWise Partners expands career opportunities for talented, motivated individuals from communities historically underrepresented in professional and leadership roles. Through career mentorship, durable skill development, professional networks, and continued career support, we help individuals build meaningful careers and advance professionally.

As StreetWise Partners approaches its 30th anniversary, we are strengthening our programs, expanding strategic partnerships, and building the financial foundation to reach more individuals across New York City and Washington, D.C.

Position Overview:

StreetWise Partners seeks an entrepreneurial, results-driven Senior Director of Philanthropy and Partnerships to lead fundraising strategy, strengthen donor relationships, and drive significant revenue growth. Reporting to the CEO, the Senior Director leads the development function and oversees an existing contributed revenue portfolio of approximately $2.6 million annually. The role will expand and diversify revenue across corporate partnerships, foundations, individual giving, government funding, and special events, with the ambitious goal of doubling contributed revenue over a multi-year period.

This leader combines strategic direction with hands-on fundraising: personally securing significant gifts, developing high-value partnerships, building donor pipelines, and coaching a high-performing team. Working with the CEO, board, and organizational leadership, the Senior Director will also lead fundraising for the 30th anniversary campaign. The position reports to Chief Executive Officer. This is a full-time hybrid role with minimum of 1 day in office in our New York City office and regular travel to Washington, D.C.

*Applications without cover letter won't be considered.

Revenue Strategy and Growth

  • Develop and execute a multi-year fundraising strategy to grow contributed revenue from the current $2.6 million base.
  • Set annual revenue targets and growth milestones across corporate, foundation, government, individual, and special event giving.
  • Diversify funding sources and build a qualified pipeline with clear cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship plans.
  • Forecast revenue, monitor performance, and adjust strategy to address gaps and emerging opportunities.
  • Expand philanthropic support in New York City, Washington, D.C., and nationally.
  • Collaborate with the CEO and operations leadership on realistic revenue projections and financial planning.

Major Gifts and Strategic Partnerships

  • Maintain an active personal portfolio of corporate, foundation, and individual prospects; personally cultivate, solicit, and close significant gifts, including six-figure and multi-year commitments.
  • Acquire new corporate partners and expand existing relationships through philanthropy, employee engagement, mentorship, and workforce development initiatives.
  • Build relationships with institutional funders; oversee competitive grant strategy, proposals, renewals, and reporting.
  • Strengthen individual giving through major gifts, annual appeals, recurring giving, and donor upgrades.
  • Leverage board, corporate, mentor, alumni, and community networks to open new funding opportunities.

Campaigns, Special Events, and Revenue Diversification

  • Lead fundraising for the 30th anniversary campaign, including goals, case for support, leadership gifts, and prospect engagement.
  • Provide strategic oversight of special events to achieve revenue goals, support cash flow, and convert attendees into engaged donors.
  • Partner with the CEO and program leadership to develop earned-revenue opportunities, including corporate workshops, mentorship initiatives, and institutional partnerships.
  • Lead relationship development and business negotiations for fee-for-service opportunities, collaborating with program and operations leaders on design, pricing, and delivery.

Development Team Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop the development team across New York City and Washington, D.C.
  • Set individual and team goals; conduct regular pipeline reviews and provide constructive performance feedback.
  • Build staff capability in prospecting, solicitation, proposal development, relationship management, and stewardship.
  • Evaluate team structure and capacity; recruit and onboard staff as organizational needs evolve.

Development Operations and Donor Stewardship

  • Oversee donor stewardship strategies that improve retention, renewals, and increased giving.
  • Ensure priority donors and corporate partners have documented relationship plans, owners, and engagement calendars.
  • Oversee Salesforce data integrity, pipeline tracking, dashboards, and reporting.

description:
AFL manufactures industry-leading fiber optic cable, connectivity and accessories and provides engineering and installation services for some of the largest telecom customers in the world. Our company was founded in 1984 with a single fiber optic cable and today, we manufacture thousands of products, generate an excess of $2B in revenue, and employ approximately 12,000 associates worldwide. About the Role
The Sustainability Specialist supports the collection, management, and reporting of AFL’s sustainability data, along with related process improvement and employee engagement initiatives. This role helps translate customer, regulatory, and stakeholder expectations into accurate data, clear reporting, and practical, repeatable processes.
Reporting to the Corporate Responsibility Manager, this position works across operations, engineering, IT, procurement, finance, marketing, and commercial teams, both in the office and on the manufacturing floor. The ideal candidate is a highly organized, self-directed professional who manages and plans their own work, coordinates input from others, and follows through to completion. They are curious, proactive, and enthusiastic about sustainability, and they bring new ideas to the team.


What You'll Do
Sustainability Data
• Own AFL’s global sustainability data used for internal and external reporting, including energy, emissions, water, waste, and production data, and maintain the platforms that hold it (e.g., EnergyCAP, Gravity).
• Prepare data for AFL’s Scope 1, 2, and 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory by collecting it from data owners across a wide range of sources, resolving gaps, and organizing it into a usable format.
• Gather, process, and validate product data for Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs), Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), and related reporting. This includes bills of materials, material mass and composition, packaging, and manufacturing data. Work with Engineering, PLM, subject matter experts, and consultants to obtain the information needed.
• Support energy projects by collecting data from equipment, departments, and sites.
• Perform quality assurance and quality control checks for completeness, units, time periods, and source traceability, and maintain issue logs and documentation to support third-party assurance.
• Lead the development of Power BI dashboards for team, leadership, and site audiences by identifying reporting needs, researching design options, and partnering with internal stakeholders and IT to deliver clear, presentation-ready dashboards.
Sustainability Reporting
• Coordinate AFL’s annual Corporate Responsibility Report, including scheduling and participating in stakeholder interviews, collecting KPI data, and following up with contributors so that data, content, and reviews are completed on schedule.
• Support third-party assessments and questionnaires, such as CDP, EcoVadis, RBA Self-Assessment Questionnaires, and customer sustainability requests, by gathering and verifying information from multiple sources and preparing evidence for owner review.
• Build and maintain repeatable processes to collect information once and reuse it across questionnaires and reports, with clear sources, owners, and traceability.
• Maintain trackers of assigned reporting tasks, owners, timelines, and status, and follow up with contributors until work is complete.
Process Improvement & Knowledge Management
• Partner with internal ETQ document control system administrators to develop and maintain the Sustainability work instruction system.
• Develop and maintain work instructions for recurring activities to support backup coverage and consistent data quality.
• Identify and help implement automation, AI, and process improvement opportunities (e.g., Copilot).
Engagement & Communications
• Update and maintain the Sustainability SharePoint site so policies, reports, and program resources are organized, engaging, and easy to find.
• Propose and coordinate employee engagement activities such as Energy Awareness Month, Earth Day, and volunteer days.
• Partner with Marketing and Communications to develop content that shares AFL’s sustainability progress.
Success Measures / KPIs
• Sustainability and product data is complete, accurate, traceable, and ready for reporting and assurance.
• Reporting milestones, assessments, and customer requests are completed accurately and on time, with risks raised early.
• Data collection processes and work instructions are documented, repeatable, and usable by others.
• Dashboards provide clear, useful visibility for team, leadership, and site audiences.
• Process improvements are identified, with approved projects implemented with measurable benefit (e.g., time saved, fewer errors).
• Engagement activities and communications are planned and delivered throughout the year.
• The Sustainability SharePoint site is current, organized, and easy to navigate.
• Work is self-managed, with clear status visibility and minimal day-to-day direction.

What Sets You Up For Success
Required
• Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, sustainability, business, engineering, or a related field.
• 1–3 years of professional experience.
• Strong organization and planning skills, including the ability to break larger projects into milestones and manage multiple priorities and deadlines with limited day-to-day direction.
• Proven ability to coordinate work across teams and achieve results without direct authority.
• Comfort working with data, including strong Excel skills (e.g., pivot tables, lookups), attention to detail, and the ability to identify errors and trace numbers to their source.
• Willingness to learn and apply digital tools, including Power BI, SharePoint, and automation and AI tools (e.g., Power Automate, Microsoft Copilot).
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including proactive status updates and early communication of risks and issues.
• Proactive and creative, with a track record of bringing forward ideas and following through on them.
• Curiosity and comfort learning technical topics and working in a manufacturing environment.
• Enthusiasm for sustainability and for engaging others.

Preferred
• Experience with GHG inventory, energy tracking, or other environmental data software.
• Experience with advance Microsoft 365 tools such as Power BI, SharePoint, Power Automate, Copilot.
• Experience developing and maintaining work instructions and document control systems (e.g. ETQ).
• Experience planning events, campaigns, or employee engagement activities.

What You Can Expect

title: Principal Engineer - Liquidity
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Principal Engineer - Liquidity based in Switzerland.

As a Principal Engineer - Liquidity, you will shape the architecture of critical financial systems that manage liquidity across multiple blockchain networks, exchanges, wallets, and bridges. You will define the technical foundations for rebalancing, pricing, risk management, and financial reporting while ensuring capital efficiency and operational reliability. Working closely with engineering leadership and quantitative developers, you will translate complex financial models into robust production systems. This is a hands-on technical leadership role combining architectural ownership, system design, prototyping, and code reviews. You will also help establish engineering standards and build the next generation of protocol-level liquidity infrastructure. The team embraces an AI-agent-driven engineering approach, using advanced tools to accelerate development while maintaining human accountability for critical decisions.

Accountabilities

You will own the technical direction of the liquidity platform, making architectural decisions that support reliability, performance, security, and future growth. You will collaborate with engineers, quantitative developers, and protocol specialists to turn complex requirements into scalable systems.

  • Define the target architecture and implementation roadmap across rebalancing, pricing, fees, risk limits, ledger and P&L, reference data, and external integrations.
  • Evaluate build-versus-reuse opportunities, select appropriate technologies, and document key architectural decisions and trade-offs.
  • Establish reliability standards for systems handling financial transactions, including idempotency, explicit state machines, reconciliation, observability, kill switches, and safe deployment practices.
  • Define and maintain strict latency budgets for critical liquidity inputs, ensuring slower processes such as ledger writes remain outside performance-sensitive request paths.
  • Lead the design of core systems, including the ledger and P&L infrastructure, reference data platform, risk engine, rebalancing state machine, and dynamic pricing capabilities.
  • Translate quantitative models into production-ready technical designs in collaboration with quantitative developers.
  • Remain hands-on by prototyping solutions, contributing code to critical system components, and reviewing high-risk changes.
  • Design protocol-level liquidity capabilities and collaborate with the Protocol team on the next generation of core infrastructure.
  • Define the requirements and components of the liquidity layer, including its dedicated infrastructure, keys, permissions, and security controls.
  • Lead architecture and design reviews, mentor senior engineers, and help raise engineering standards across the team.
  • Replace one-off partner integrations with reusable configuration and shared tooling to simplify the launch of new partners and blockchain networks.
  • Contribute to technical hiring and help build the engineering team responsible for these systems.

Requirements

You are an experienced technical leader with a strong background in backend and distributed systems, particularly in environments where technical failures can have direct financial consequences. You combine architectural vision with practical engineering skills, understand the importance of correctness and performance in financial infrastructure, and can guide technical decisions without relying on formal management authority.

  • 10+ years of experience building backend or distributed systems, including several years in a Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, or Architect role with ownership of architecture across multiple systems.
  • Proven experience building and operating systems involving real-money transactions, such as trading platforms, exchanges, payment infrastructure, treasury systems, ledgers, or market-making solutions.
  • Deep understanding of financial system correctness, including ledgers, double-entry accounting, idempotency, state machines, reconciliation, and handling partial failures across external systems.
  • Experience designing and operating systems with strict request-path latency requirements, ideally in the single-digit millisecond range or below.
  • Strong understanding of performance optimization across runtime, memory, networking, and storage.
  • Production-level experience with at least one of the following technologies: TypeScript/Node.js, Rust, Java/Kotlin, or Go.
  • A track record of producing clear architectural and design documentation that has been adopted across multiple teams.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts, build consensus, and influence engineering direction without direct managerial responsibility.
  • Hands-on approach to engineering, including prototyping, coding critical components, reviewing complex changes, and validating technical decisions.
  • Ability to prioritize pragmatic solutions, sequence development effectively, and deliver value without compromising long-term architecture.
  • Experience using AI agents to explore designs, generate and test code, and validate technical reasoning, with the ability to critically review their output.
  • Strong interest in blockchain technology, cryptocurrency, and the engineering challenges of cross-chain liquidity.

Nice To Have

  • Experience with blockchain bridges, automated market makers (AMMs), exchange APIs, custody and key management, cross-chain settlement, solvers, or intent-based systems.
  • Experience developing smart contracts for liquidity pools using Solidity.
  • Experience migrating systems to dedicated infrastructure with separate accounts, keys, permissions, and access controls.

Location and availability:

  • Remote position with at least three hours of overlap with the 08:00–17:00 UTC working window.
  • Candidates must be located outside jurisdictions excluded by global exchange eligibility requirements, including the United States and Canada.

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary.
  • Equity package.
  • Comprehensive health benefits.
  • Unlimited paid time off, with an encouraged minimum.
  • Remote-first working environment.
  • Flexible culture focused on collaboration, clear communication, and autonomy.

title: Product Manager, US Marketing, Hematology
description:

  • Self-starter with a “roll-up-your-sleeves” approach and the ability to adapt to evolving business needs

$115,200.00---$172,800.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.


When you join Genmab, you’re joining a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional wellness. Within the first year, regular full-time U.S. employees are eligible for:

  • Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

title: Science & Technology Project Leader, Autonomous Lab Accelerator
description:
The Position

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.


Advances in AI, data, robotics, and laboratory automation are transforming drug discovery and development. The Roche Autonomous Lab Accelerator brings together multiple disciplines across the organization to build closed-loop Lab-in-the-Loop capabilities that connect scientific intent, experimental execution, analysis, and high-quality data generation.



The Opportunity


As a Science & Technology Project Leader within Automation Science & Technology, you will lead the scientific definition and delivery of priority autonomous experimentation workflows across the Roche Autonomous Lab Accelerator. This role reports to the Head, Automation Science & Technology, Autonomous Lab Accelerator. You will work across scientific teams to understand and harmonize workflow needs, challenge existing approaches where appropriate, and translate scientific requirements into automation-ready workflows. A successful individual in this role owns scientific readiness and acceptance of the delivered workflow, and will work closely with scientific SMEs, Lab Automation, Lab Operations, and CS CoE, you will drive development of solutions that balance scientific needs, automation feasibility, operational readiness, and AI/informatics requirements.


In this role, you will:


Key Responsibilities


  • Scientific Workflow Definition: Understand scientific workflows across different groups and divisions; align common requirements; identify gaps, unnecessary variation, and opportunities for standardization; and define automation-ready scientific workflows.
  • Scientific Readiness & Requirements: Work with scientific SMEs to define methods, controls, assay parameters, process steps, decision points, data requirements, and acceptance criteria. Establish deadlines and hold SMEs accountable for delivering stable requirements on time.
  • Cross-Functional Solution Development: Partner with Lab Automation, Lab Operations, and computational and informatics teams to develop solutions that meet scientific needs while remaining technically feasible, operationally supportable, and scalable.
  • AI-Native Workflow Design: Define workflows that connect experimental design, execution, structured data generation, analysis, and model feedback to support increasingly closed-loop experimentation.
  • Scientific Project Leadership: Lead scientific delivery from use-case definition through implementation, managing milestones, dependencies, risks, and decisions across scientific and technical teams.
  • Scientific Acceptance & Handoff: Own scientific acceptance of the delivered workflow, remain accountable through an initial stabilization period, and then transition ongoing scientific ownership to the appropriate scientific or business organization.
  • Strategic Alignment: Identify opportunities to reuse workflows, standards, and platform capabilities across the broader Autonomous Lab Accelerator portfolio and across organizational boundaries.

Key Deliverables


  • Automation-ready scientific workflow and requirements
  • Scientific readiness plan with SME commitments and milestones
  • Integrated solution aligned across science, automation, operations, and informatics
  • AI-native data and workflow requirements supporting closed-loop experimentation
  • Scientific acceptance of the implemented capability
  • Stabilization and transition to long-term scientific ownership
  • Reusable workflow patterns and lessons learned across Accelerator projects

Who you are


  • Advanced degree in a relevant scientific discipline with significant experience in small or large molecule drug discovery, experimental sciences, or scientific technology.
  • Broad scientific knowledge and the ability to understand, challenge, and integrate diverse scientific workflows.
  • Strong systems thinking with attention to detail in workflow steps, controls, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across scientific, engineering, informatics, and operational organizations.
  • Strong execution discipline, including setting timelines, resolving ambiguity, managing dependencies, and holding collaborators accountable.
  • Good understanding of laboratory automation, experimental data, and AI/ML-enabled scientific workflows.
  • Clear communicator who can translate across technical and scientific audiences.
  • Strategic thinker who can connect individual projects to broader organizational priorities and reusable Autonomous Lab Accelerator capabilities.

Relocation benefits are NOT available for this job posting

title: Senior Electrical Pre Construction Engineer
description:
TSL - About Us


TSL is a leading international technical engineering and construction partner operating across the UK, Ireland, and Mainland Europe. We focus on design and build contracts for end user clients, specialising in the Food, Pharmaceutical, Logistics, Data Centre and Advanced Manufacturing sectors.


TSL is committed to creating the spaces that enable the fourth industrial revolution, whilst ensuring we leave a positive environmental and social legacy for communities across the world. Our team work with our valued clients and supply chain partners to create a simple agenda concentrated on getting things done. Above all, we are focused on delivering first class projects, executed efficiently, without compromising on safety or quality.


TSL’s recent growth has created several exciting new opportunities for the organization to address. One of these is investing in steadily growing TSL’s Finance Team core capability and influence across the organization to support the rapid expansion across the globe.


The opportunity


TSL is seeking a Senior Electrical Pre-Construction Engineer to lead electrical pre-construction activity across complex, fast-paced projects, with a strong focus on data centers. Based in Kildare, this role offers substantial travel, typically one to two international project visits per month, alongside opportunities to support work across Ireland.


Drawing on TSL’s Organization Context, this role supports the delivery of high-performance turnkey facilities for global clients while maintaining the company’s priorities of safety, quality, schedule certainty, sustainability, and technical excellence.


What you’ll do


• Lead and coordinate electrical pre-construction activities across multiple live tenders and project opportunities.

• Support electrical design development, design management, technical reviews, and coordination with internal and external design partners.

What you’ll bring


  • qualifications or equivalent in Electrical Engineering.

• Strong communication and leadership skills, with the ability to guide teams and build productive relationships with clients, consultants, vendors, and delivery partners.

You will bring structure and technical leadership to pre-construction work, helping teams develop coordinated, buildable, commercially aware electrical solutions. You will enable TSL to progress projects at speed without compromising safety, quality, or client outcomes, while strengthening long-term partnerships across international markets.

title: Credentialing & Contracting Specialist
description:
Contracting & Credentialing Specialist
Location: Remote (U.S.-based)
Department: Healthcare Operations
Reports To: COO
Schedule: Full-time


About Ladder Health

Ladder Health is reimagining early childhood developmental care by delivering proactive, holistic, and family-centered support for children with or at risk of developmental delays. Built in collaboration with Boston Children’s Hospital, our virtual-first care model brings together expert clinicians (PT, OT, and SLP), thoughtful technology, and a powerful belief: that every child deserves the chance to thrive.

We partner with pediatricians, health systems, and payers to close access gaps and offer personalized care for families across the developmental spectrum—meeting them wherever they are, whenever they need us.


About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Contracting & Credentialing Specialist to manage and scale our provider credentialing, payer enrollment, and contract maintenance operations. This role is critical to ensuring our clinicians are fully and efficiently credentialed across markets and key commercial and Medicaid payers so that families can get access to in-network, expert care, fast.

As a key member of the Healthcare Operations team, you will directly manage and execute all provider credentialing, re-credentialing, payer enrollment (including CAQH maintenance), and contract updates, including negotiations related to fee schedules and enrollments. You will work closely with Revenue Cycle Management, Practice Operations, clinical teams, and payer representatives to streamline operational workflows and hand-offs to ensure you can seamlessly execute all contracting and credentialing tasks.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who is mission-oriented, thrives in a fast-paced startup environment, and is excited to take ownership of building scalable systems.


What You’ll Do

Credentialing & Payer Enrollment

  • Lead provider credentialing and re-credentialing processes across multiple commercial and Medicaid payers, ensuring timely approvals and regulatory compliance
  • Manage payer enrollment, meeting or exceeding all company-defined SLAs, and maintain accurate records of provider participation status
  • Work directly with clinicians (PT, OT, SLP) to maintain accurate, up-to-date provider rosters, license documentation, and CAQH profiles.
  • Ensure smooth operational hand-offs between practice ops, clinical teams, and billing/RCM partners (including external vendors).

Payer Contracting & Fee Schedule Management

  • Support the negotiation and execution of new payer contracts as well as securing updated fee schedules and rate increases on existing contracts
  • Negotiate delegated credentialing agreements upfront or during contract renegotiation cycles to reduce enrollment timelines.
  • Track contract expiration dates, renewal timelines, and payer fee schedule updates to maximize reimbursement performance
  • Serve as the primary liaison for payer relations, network management, and contracting inquiries

Document, Optimize & Automate Key Processes

  • Document standard operating procedures and guidelines for provider credentialing, payer enrollment, and re-credentialing workflows
  • Identify operational bottlenecks and continuously optimize credentialing timelines and intake verification processes
  • Implement and maintain workflow tools (including approved, HIPAA-compliant AI tools) to reduce manual work in credentialing and contracting


Who You Are

  • 4+ years in provider credentialing and payer enrollment, with direct exposure to or ownership of payer contracting
  • Strong knowledge of commercial and Medicaid payer credentialing requirements, CAQH, and payer portals
  • Experience working with therapy or pediatric outpatient services (PT/OT/SLP) or similar specialties (preferred)
  • Proficiency with EHR/EMR systems, clearinghouses, and payer portals
  • Hands-on self-starter with proven experience building systems and operational infrastructure from the ground up, in a fast-paced startup environment
  • High level of comfort applying technology in innovative ways, plus experience with workflow optimization and automation tools
  • Highly organized, analytical, detail-oriented, and process-driven. Knows how to prioritize work around critical efforts versus first in, first out.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across teams and explain complex concepts clearly
  • Passionate about improving access to care for children and families


Nice to Haves

  • Experience in a virtual care environment
  • Experience negotiating and executing delegated credentialing agreements
  • Experience negotiating fee schedule increases with health plans
  • Experience building and/or applying AI solutions to credentialing operations
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish or English/Portuguese)


Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on experience
  • Equity package
  • Flexible, remote-first work environment
  • Opportunity to shape and scale a critical function within a high-growth company
  • Mission-driven team focused on improving pediatric developmental care

title: Salesforce Consultant - DevOps Speciality
description:
About Trideca

Trideca is Australia's trusted strategy, AI, and digital transformation partner, helping some of the nation's largest enterprises (including NAB, Suncorp, Optus, Medibank, and AGL) drive meaningful business impact through technology.

With offices in Melbourne and Sydney and projects spanning multiple industries, we thrive on solving complex challenges, delivering cutting-edge solutions, and pushing the boundaries of what's possible.

About the role

Trideca is seeking a Salesforce DevOps Lead to join a leading Australian health organisation and move its Salesforce delivery from manual Change Sets to a governed GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline. You will own the path from mobilisation and target design through the Git baseline, pipeline build, quality and security gates, pilot migration and handover, and you will be the technical authority on how Salesforce change is versioned, tested, approved and released across multiple orgs.

This is a consulting role with your hands on the platform. You will build the workflows, write the Salesforce CLI scripts and fix the failing tests yourself, not only specify them. By handover, the client's own developers and administrators will be running the pipeline with confidence, because you will have taught them how.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Lead mobilisation, discovery and target design workshops with platform, security, architecture and release stakeholders, and turn the findings into a sequenced delivery plan, backlog and acceptance criteria.
  • Establish a Git repository and Salesforce DX project baseline for each org, retrieving and cleaning production metadata so Git becomes the source of truth.
  • Move credentials out of Custom Labels and Custom Metadata into an enterprise secrets vault and Named Credentials before the first commit, with OIDC authentication, push protection, secret rotation and an integration registry in place.
  • Build GitHub Actions workflows for validation, delta packaging, deployment and rollback using Salesforce CLI and sfdx-git-delta, promoting every change through controlled environments.
  • Implement the branching model, pull request controls and branch protection, with Jira traceability from story to commit to release.
  • Build the automated test framework and quality gates: fix failing Apex tests, add Jest for Lightning Web Components and Playwright end to end tests, and report results through Xray.
  • Add DevSecOps scanning and policy gates, including Salesforce Code Analyzer and secret scanning, and capture the audit evidence a regulated organisation needs.
  • Set up environment controls covering sandbox refresh schedules, drift detection and post refresh safety steps that stop sandboxes sending communications or calling production integrations.
  • Partner with architects, security, release managers and the Change Advisory Board on approval gates, the release calendar, naming conventions and engineering standards, and own the runbooks, environment maps and rollback procedures behind them.
  • Lead the pilot migration, parallel run and cutover from Change Sets, then train and mentor developers and administrators as they move to Git, VS Code and pull requests.
  • Advise how the same controls extend to Marketing Cloud, Data 360 and a future Health Cloud implementation, where deployment tooling differs from the core platform.

What You Bring

  • Eight or more years in Salesforce platform delivery, including at least three years hands on building and running Salesforce CI/CD pipelines.
  • Leadership of at least one end to end move from Change Sets to Git based source control and automated deployment, across multiple orgs in an enterprise environment.
  • Salesforce Platform Developer I or Administrator certification, current or equivalent, with delivery depth to match.
  • Deep hands on capability with Salesforce DX, Salesforce CLI, the Metadata API, sandbox strategy and delta deployments.
  • Strong GitHub and GitHub Actions experience, including reusable workflows, environments and approvals, branch protection, runners and OIDC.
  • Secrets management for Salesforce, including an enterprise vault, Named Credentials and JWT based authentication for pipelines.
  • Test automation across Apex, Jest for Lightning Web Components and Playwright or an equivalent UI framework, enforced through quality gates, alongside static analysis with Salesforce Code Analyzer or PMD and secret scanning in the pipeline.
  • Release and change governance in a regulated environment, including Change Advisory Board approvals, release calendars, rollback and audit evidence.
  • Working knowledge of Sales Cloud, Service Cloud and Marketing Cloud, enough to understand what each team builds and how it is deployed.
  • Confident workshop facilitation, stakeholder engagement and training delivery, with the ability to produce clear designs and documentation.
  • Australian working rights and the ability to work hybrid from a client site.

Nice to Have

  • Salesforce Certified Platform Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect.
  • Marketing Cloud Engagement deployment tooling such as Accenture SFMC DevTools (mcdev), and Data 360 DevOps data kits.
  • Health Cloud delivery, or experience working with health information under the Privacy Act and APRA CPS 234.
  • Commercial Salesforce DevOps tools such as Gearset, Copado or Salesforce DevOps Center.
  • Scratch orgs, unlocked packages and trunk based development.
  • Migration of Process Builder and Workflow Rules to Flow.
  • Experience setting up a shared Salesforce platform practice or centre of excellence.

Why Choose Trideca?

Empowering Women in Technology: We are committed to closing the gender gap in technology. With our dedicated road map for women, you'll find tailored opportunities to advance your career, supported by mentorship, leadership programs, Women in Technology Chapter and inclusive policies like menstruation leave and flexible working options.

Growth Through Learning: Your growth is our priority. At Trideca, you'll have access to a wide range of learning and development initiatives, from certifications and workshops to personal development programs, ensuring you are always at the forefront of technology and innovation.

Work Your Way: Our flexible work policy supports you to balance your personal and professional life.

Trideca Values

Clients Come First
